claims.text: When inefficient queries coincide with CPU or I/O pressure, inspect query samples, targeting and execution plans and evaluate index improvements. Atlas also documents increasing hardware resources as a valid immediate response; the evidence does not support a blanket claim that scaling first always wastes budget or that ESR alone resolves the bottleneck. (medium confidence)

Atlas triage starts by matching the incident time to historical latency or service objectives, recent application or deployment changes, node health, and CPU, IOPS, connection, and memory evidence; correlate these signals before assigning a root cause. (high confidence)

For high disk I/O, compare observed IOPS with provisioned IOPS and inspect IOWait alongside latency and query activity. Unoptimized queries and index builds can trigger I/O alerts; query optimization and additional IOPS or compute are possible responses, so resource symptoms alone do not establish a checkpoint-specific cause. (high confidence)

The self-managed diagnostics FAQ defines the default WiredTiger internal cache as the larger of 50% of (RAM minus 1 GB) and 0.256 GB. It separately describes filesystem caching and other RAM consumers. This formula corrects the legacy shorthand '50% RAM' but does not prove the effective cache allocation of every Atlas tier. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

For I/O triage, compare observed disk IOPS with provisioned IOPS and inspect CPU IOWait, then investigate slow queries and index builds. These observations identify I/O pressure; the reviewed sources do not establish queued WiredTiger checkpoints as a necessary signature of cloud-provider throttling. (medium confidence)

Memory triage should distinguish WiredTiger cache, filesystem cache, swap and workload behavior. The reviewed passages do not establish a universal greater-than-90%-memory failure condition, a universal 1 MB-per-thread connection cost, or maxConns and allowDiskUse as a general Atlas remedy. (medium confidence)

A July 1, 2026 Nimbly investigation combines Atlas activity events, per-node connection metrics and application logs to construct a failover timeline. Its attribution of maintenance failure and retry amplification is the author's interpretation, and it explicitly requests MongoDB's official RCA; use the evidence-correlation method without treating the attribution as vendor-confirmed. (low confidence)

A useful investigation sequence is to move from cluster and replication health to slow operations and explain plans, then correlate application and infrastructure context. Datadog describes this workflow for MongoDB including Atlas; Atlas documentation independently recommends metric review and query/index investigation. (medium confidence)

Before treating slow queries as a pure capacity problem, inspect representative execution plans for collection scans, excessive documents examined, and unsupported sorts; improve indexes or query shape and verify latency and work performed afterward. Scaling remains an option when optimized queries still saturate resources. (high confidence)

RTPP exposes CPU percentage, disk read/write IOPS, system memory, current operations and query-targeting ratios; Atlas architecture guidance documents one-second UI granularity. Historical Metrics charts are a separate surface with coarser collection and aggregation intervals. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

For a lost-primary alert on an election-based replica set, check CPU, IOPS, and connection exhaustion first. If resource metrics are normal, investigate cloud-network disruption; Atlas attempts repair and persistent failures require MongoDB Support. An alert collected during an election can be a false positive, so configure its waiting interval accordingly. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

A first-person Atlas incident account dated June 22, 2023 correlates a scheduled analytical query with disk-utilization and profiler spikes. The operator reports improved query latency after retention cleanup and warns that the cleanup itself raised CPU load and reduced the oplog window. This is a reported case, not a universal diagnosis. (low confidence)

RTPP presents current operations and host hardware statistics at one-second granularity. Its CPU, Disk IOPS, and Sys Mem fields describe CPU percentage, disk read/write operations per second, and physical memory usage excluding buffers and swap; the reviewed RTPP reference does not label this CPU field as normalized. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Stored cluster metrics normally use one-minute collection, with replication lag and headroom collected at 85 seconds. A project with at least one M40-or-larger cluster receives ten-second premium collection. Coarser normal metrics average finer reports, while burst equivalents retain maxima; use Max metrics and a narrower incident window to investigate spikes hidden by averages. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Memory triage must allow for filesystem cache and consumers outside the WiredTiger internal cache, including connections and aggregation or sort work. Percona warns that configuring an excessively large WiredTiger cache can contribute to OOM; MongoDB likewise advises against increasing the default internal cache without justification. (high confidence)
